_comment: Golden set for Sung et al. 2021 — Global Cancer Statistics 2020 (GLOBOCAN). Claims annotated by reading the source PDF directly. Covers abstract, results, and discussion sections. Paper ingested as p_000001.
claims: Worldwide, an estimated 19.3 million new cancer cases and almost 10.0 million cancer deaths occurred in 2020.
Female breast cancer has surpassed lung cancer as the most commonly diagnosed cancer globally in 2020, with an estimated 2.3 million new cases (11.7%).
Lung cancer remained the leading cause of cancer death globally in 2020, with an estimated 1.8 million deaths (18%).
The global cancer burden is expected to reach 28.4 million cases in 2040, a 47% rise from 2020.
Cancer is the first or second leading cause of premature death before age 70 in 112 of 183 countries.
Overall cancer incidence was 2-fold to 3-fold higher in transitioned versus transitioning countries for both sexes.
Asia accounted for approximately 49.3% of all cancer cases and 58.3% of cancer deaths globally in 2020.
One in 5 men or women will develop cancer in their lifetime, and 1 in 8 men and 1 in 11 women will die from it.
Approximately two-thirds of lung cancer deaths worldwide are attributable to smoking.
HBV infection and HCV infection account for 56% and 20% of liver cancer deaths worldwide, respectively.
Cervical cancer incidence rates remain disproportionately high in transitioning versus transitioned countries (18.8 vs 11.3 per 100,000).
As of May 2020, less than 30% of LMICs had implemented national HPV vaccination programs, compared with over 80% of high-income countries.
Low HDI countries are projected to see a 95% increase in cancer cases by 2040, and medium HDI countries a 64% increase.
